Querying human gene annotation via biocOnIce with org.Hs.eg.ice

Bioconductor Core Team

2026-10-22

Source: vignettes/org.Hs.eg.ice.qmd

Overview

org.Hs.eg.ice is a demonstration package: human gene annotation served from the biocOnIce public Iceberg catalog, queried directly with dplyr/DBI, with no dependency on AnnotationDbi – no OrgDb class, no Bimap objects, no select()/mapIds()/keytypes() keytype whitelist. See PlanFor3.24.md Milestone 7 in the BioconductorAnnotationPipeline repository for the design rationale, and Milestone 8 for the local-caching layer shown below.

All code below runs live against the anonymous, unauthenticated biocOnIce endpoint at build time, except one chunk flagged eval: false where it’s explicitly noted why (a full cache refresh including the ~6.6M-row alias table takes ~15 minutes – too slow for a vignette build, though the code itself is exercised elsewhere with skip_alias = TRUE).

library(org.Hs.eg.ice)
library(dplyr)

The four accessors

Each accessor is a lazy dplyr table, already filtered to human (taxon_id = 9606) and to currently-valid rows. Nothing else – every join, every column selection, is ordinary dplyr written by the caller.

  • hs_gene() – annotation.ncbi__gene: gene_id, symbol, description, gene_type, chromosome, map_location.
  • hs_alias() – annotation.identifier_mapping: every cross-reference namespace NCBI/Ensembl assert, discriminated by source_namespace/ target_namespace.
  • hs_go() – annotation.ncbi__gene_go: direct GO annotations, go_id/ evidence/qualifier/category.
  • hs_pubmed() – annotation.ncbi__gene_pubmed: gene_id/pubmed_id.

The comparison that motivates this package

The AnnotationDbi way:

library(org.Hs.eg.db)
mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db, keys = "TP53", keytype = "SYMBOL", column = "ENTREZID")
  TP53
"7157" 
select(org.Hs.eg.db, keys = "TP53", keytype = "SYMBOL",
       columns = c("ENTREZID", "GENENAME"))
  SYMBOL ENTREZID          GENENAME
1   TP53     7157 tumor protein p53

The direct way:

org.Hs.eg.db loads AnnotationDbi, whose select() masks dplyr::select() – qualify explicitly as dplyr::select() from here on in a session that has both packages loaded.

hs_gene() |>
    filter(symbol == "TP53") |>
    dplyr::select(gene_id, symbol, description) |>
    collect()

GOALL: the GO ancestor closure as a recursive CTE

OrgDb’s GOALL (the ancestor closure over the GO DAG) needs ontology.relationship, a table this package does not wrap – attach it directly, as bioc-on-ice’s own README shows for cell types.

A CTE (common table expression) is a named, temporary result set defined with WITH name AS (...) immediately before the query that uses it. WITH RECURSIVE lets the CTE refer to itself, so the query below starts from one gene’s direct GO terms and repeatedly joins back into ontology.relationship to pick up each term’s is_a parents, one level of the DAG at a time, until no new ancestors are found:

con <- ice_con()
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
    WITH RECURSIVE ancestors(go_id) AS (
        SELECT go_id FROM bioc.annotation.ncbi__gene_go
        WHERE gene_id = '7157' AND taxon_id = 9606 AND valid_to IS NULL
        UNION
        SELECT r.object_id
        FROM bioc.ontology.relationship r
        JOIN ancestors a ON r.subject_id = a.go_id
        WHERE r.predicate = 'is_a' AND r.ontology = 'go' AND r.valid_to IS NULL
    )
    SELECT DISTINCT t.term_id, t.name
    FROM ancestors a
    JOIN bioc.ontology.term t ON t.term_id = a.go_id AND t.valid_to IS NULL;
") |>
    head(10)
      term_id                                                             name
1  GO:2000379 positive regulation of reactive oxygen species metabolic process
2  GO:0005654                                                      nucleoplasm
3  GO:0070245               positive regulation of thymocyte apoptotic process
4  GO:1990841                              promoter-specific chromatin binding
5  GO:0006974                                              DNA damage response
6  GO:0000122        negative regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II
7  GO:0005829                                                          cytosol
8  GO:0030330   DNA damage response, signal transduction by p53 class mediator
9  GO:0042981                                  regulation of apoptotic process
10 GO:0032991                                       protein-containing complex

That query is exactly what GOALL/select(..., columns = "GOALL") can never return in one AnnotationDbi call – this package doesn’t need to invent an API for it, because the recursive CTE is already SQL.

Local caching (provisional, Milestone 8)

Every accessor above stays live by default. Live-catalog latency is real – a single filtered query over the network can take seconds, dominated by S3/catalog metadata overhead rather than result size (PlanFor3.24.md Milestone 8 measured 0.099s against org.Hs.eg.db locally versus 4.15s against a live hs_gene()/hs_pubmed() join). If that’s a problem for a session, ice_cache_refresh() pulls all four tables once into a local BiocFileCache-managed DuckDB file; pass cache = TRUE to any accessor to read from it instead.

The alias/identifier_mapping table dominates refresh time – 6.59M rows, ~740s on its own – versus well under two minutes combined for gene, go, and pubmed. A full refresh is too slow to run at vignette build time, so it’s shown but not evaluated here:

ice_cache_refresh()                       # one-time, explicit, ~15 minutes

skip_alias = TRUE omits that table and keeps the refresh well under two minutes – this does run at build time:

system.time(ice_cache_refresh(skip_alias = TRUE))

A real end-to-end run (full refresh, alias included) measured 0.090s cached versus 15.987s live for a hs_gene()/hs_pubmed() join on this same gene – about 178x. hs_alias(cache = TRUE) errors cleanly when alias was skipped:

hs_alias(cache = TRUE)

ice_cache_clear()
ice_cache_exists()

Nothing calls ice_cache_refresh() automatically, and nothing expires the cache automatically – call it again when you want a fresher copy, or ice_cache_clear() to remove it.

This caching layer is provisional: it does not yet tag the cache with a bioc-on-ice provenance.release identifier, and makes no cross-table-consistency claim beyond what the live catalog itself provides. See PlanFor3.24.md Milestone 8’s open caveat on cross-table atomicity – row-level versioning is applied per table independently, so filtering hs_gene() and hs_pubmed() to “the same” nominal release does not, by itself, prove a join between them is point-in-time consistent.

AnnotationDbi concept → org.Hs.eg.ice equivalent

AnnotationDbi concept (org.Hs.eg.db) org.Hs.eg.db org.Hs.eg.ice
Object model OrgDb S4 class, Bimap objects under the hood No class at all – four plain dplyr::tbl() lazy tables
keytypes(x) Fixed whitelist (ENTREZID, SYMBOL, ALIAS, ENSEMBL, GO, PMID, …) No such function. “Keytype” is whichever column you filter() on – e.g. hs_alias() |> filter(target_namespace == "ALIAS") is OrgDb’s ALIAS keytype
columns(x) Fixed list of retrievable columns No enumeration function – the columns are whatever’s in the four tables’ schemas
select(x, keys, keytype, columns) One call does filter + column choice + join Ordinary dplyr::filter() + select() + left_join()/inner_join() written by the caller
mapIds(x, keys, keytype, column) Single-valued lookup with multiVals logic No equivalent; filter()+select()+collect(), caller handles 1:many
ENTREZID Row names / keytype hs_gene()$gene_id
SYMBOL keytype/column hs_gene()$symbol
GENENAME column hs_gene()$description
GENETYPE column hs_gene()$gene_type
CHR column hs_gene()$chromosome
MAP column hs_gene()$map_location
ALIAS, ENSEMBL, HGNC, MIM, … separate keytypes, each its own internal table all rows of hs_alias(), discriminated by source_namespace/target_namespace
GO (direct) column hs_go(): go_id, evidence, qualifier, category
GOALL (ancestor closure) precomputed column hand-written WITH RECURSIVE CTE over ontology.relationship/ontology.term (above)
PMID column hs_pubmed()$pubmed_id
Multi-table joins not expressible in one call ordinary dplyr joins across the four lazy tables
Offline / cold-start speed instant, local SQLite, ~0.1s/query live: ~4-16s/query; cached: ~0.09s/query
Local caching implicit (the package is a local cache) opt-in ice_cache_refresh() + cache = TRUE (above)
Versioning / reproducibility pinned to installed package version not yet addressed by the cache; open cross-table-atomicity question (Milestone 8)
Dependencies AnnotationDbi, RSQLite, Bioconductor infrastructure DBI, dbplyr, dplyr, duckdb, BiocFileCache (cache only) – no AnnotationDbi

Status

Tests exist: tests/testthat/test-accessors.R has live-catalog tests (skips cleanly if the catalog is unreachable) and offline signature/cache-state checks. Not yet R CMD checked against the live catalog, not published. This vignette’s code runs live at build time (the only exception is cache-refresh-full above, flagged eval: false because a full refresh takes ~15 minutes).
